correctness.rationale: For each order 4 through 10, all unlabeled rooted trees arise uniquely as multisets of smaller rooted trees. Canonical one- or two-center codes identify all unlabeled free trees. For each one of the 106 ten-vertex trees the checker enumerates all 2^9 spanning-edge subsets and obtains integer component-size histograms independently via union-find and graph traversal. The rank-five signatures have exactly one two-element collision class; rank six has no collision. The two explicit representatives have diameters 6 and 7 and rank-six component partition (4,2,2,2) counts 1 and 0. Counts for lower orders certify the first strict boundary. No large-order theorem follows.

evidence: Zeng, arXiv:2608.18179, Theorem 1.1 and Section 4 proves reconstruction in multiplicity-isolated proper trees and gives a diameter-six canonical model using the full component table.
Awan, arXiv:2609.13464 Theorem 3 proves lower bounds but no upper cutoff for tau(10).
broader_coverage.reasoning: Stronger full-CSF reconstruction in a restricted subclass cannot give a statement about all 106 trees at truncation level five. Neither inspected preprint settles which shallow rank separates every ten-vertex tree. In particular, the two diameters of the colliding pair do not imply an equality of complete chromatic symmetric functions.

evidence: Awan, arXiv:2609.13464, pp. 2–3 defines the exact connected-partition vector sigma_t and tau(k), with tau(5)=2 and lower bound floor(k/2).

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The edge-subset-component multiset, the truncated power-sum coefficient sequence, and sigma_t all encode the same rank-layer counts for trees because signs are fixed by the number of selected edges. Awan is therefore a direct-equivalence match for the definition and prior lower bound, but its inspected Section 4 does not compute order ten or the first strict rank. Searches of those equivalent terms did not locate the exact finite gap.

The inspected source manuscripts contain no 106-tree sigma5 collision table or tau(10) computation; Zeng notes a separate supplemental full-invariant cut-partition evaluator.

originality.rationale: Awan, arXiv:2609.13464, defines exactly this invariant and proves tau(k)>=floor(k/2) (k>=4), giving tau(5)=2, but not the first strict value. Zeng, arXiv:2608.18179, supplies full component-table reconstruction for particular proper-tree classes, not rank-six injectivity across all 106 ten-vertex trees. Exact-boundary and equivalent-formulation queries, plus published-record comparisons, found no covering statement. Residual risk from unindexed or supplementary computation is genuine.
residual_risks: A previously published but unindexed numerical census, code supplement, or a differently named truncated power-sum table might include the exact ten-vertex obstruction.
The claim covers only finite tree orders through ten and says nothing about all larger orders.
No independent external scientific audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The exact first order at which a recent, mathematically motivated lower bound ceases to be sharp is a natural finite cutoff, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The unique colliding ten-vertex pair identifies the precise obstruction to rank-five reconstruction and illustrates that even tree diameter can be hidden by low-rank connected-partition data. The complete 106-object classification supplies a reproducible benchmark for future reconstruction-depth work; no general theorem is claimed.
